ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Thompson-Epstein classification: 2

Following posterior hip dislocation, CT identifies one large posterior acetabular wall fragment. The wall is not extensively comminuted and the femoral head is intact. Which Thompson-Epstein grade matches this fracture-dislocation pattern?

  1. Thompson-Epstein I
  2. Thompson-Epstein III
  3. Thompson-Epstein IV
  4. Thompson-Epstein V
  5. Thompson-Epstein II
Answer and explanation

Thompson-Epstein II

Posterior dislocation accompanies a single large posterior acetabular wall fragment.

Option explanations

Thompson-Epstein II: Posterior dislocation accompanies a single large posterior acetabular wall fragment.

Thompson-Epstein I: Posterior hip dislocation has no significant acetabular fracture or only a minor fragment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein III: Posterior dislocation accompanies a comminuted posterior acetabular wall fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein IV: Posterior dislocation is associated with fracture of the acetabular floor. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein V: Posterior dislocation is associated with femoral head fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
